title: Interactive charts expose a keyboard traversal path with a stable announced-string contract
asA: keyboard-only user reading an interactive chart
iWant: each data point to be focus-reachable in reading order with a stable announced string carrying series name, x-value, y-value and unit
soThat: the pointer-only granular data-point access is available to a keyboard user (WCAG 2.1.1)

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given an interactive chart (data points are clickable or hoverable and trigger a callback), keyboard focus reaches each data point in reading order (left-to-right, top-to-bottom for single-series; series-by-series for multi-series), and the announced string on focus matches the format `<seriesName>, <xValue>, <yValue> <unit>` (comma-separated, unit is the operator-configured unit or `unitless`). A `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` media query on the rendered surface suppresses chart entry and update transitions (`transition-duration: 0` or `animation-duration: 0` on the affected elements). Probed by the application-charts pack check AC-18104-1 (Playwright drives the browser, tabs through the chart, asserts every data point receives focus, the announced string matches the format, and the reduced-motion CSS rule applies).
acceptanceCriteria.given: an interactive chart with reduced-motion respect
acceptanceCriteria.when: the operator tabs through the chart with prefers-reduced-motion set
acceptanceCriteria.then: each data point receives focus in reading order, the announced string matches the format, and transitions are suppressed

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given a non-interactive chart (no data-point activation), the keyboard-traversal AC does not apply; the chart is still tab-reachable as one focusable landmark exposing an accessible name (the chart's title or aria-label). The pack records applicable false for AC-18104-1 on a non-interactive chart; the reduced-motion rule still applies and is a separate observation on the pack record when the surface exposes any transition.
acceptanceCriteria.then: the AC-18104-1 keyboard-traversal rule does not apply and the pack records applicable false

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given an interactive chart, when the keyboard focus reaches a data point, the announced string contract reads `<series name>, <x value>, <y value> <unit>` in that order (comma or space separated); a chart whose announcement omits the series name on a multi-series chart or omits the unit fails the pack check.
acceptanceCriteria.given: keyboard focus on a data point in an interactive multi-series chart
acceptanceCriteria.when: the pack captures the announced string
acceptanceCriteria.then: the string reads `<series name>, <x value>, <y value> <unit>`; an omitted series or unit fails

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given an interactive multi-series chart, the keyboard traversal moves series-by-series (all points on series 1 in x order, then all points on series 2 in x order, and so on); a chart whose traversal moves in x-first order across all series (a zig-zag pattern) fails the pack check per REQ-004's series-by-series reading order.
acceptanceCriteria.given: keyboard traversal on an interactive multi-series chart
acceptanceCriteria.when: the pack captures the focus order
acceptanceCriteria.then: traversal is series-by-series in x order; an x-first zig-zag fails

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given an interactive chart under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, the entry and update transitions of the chart honour zero-duration (no animated tween, no easing curve); a chart whose entry animation still fires under reduced-motion fails the pack check per REQ-004 and ADR-1903.
acceptanceCriteria.given: an interactive chart under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce
acceptanceCriteria.when: the pack inspects entry and update transitions
acceptanceCriteria.then: transitions honour zero duration; an animated entry under reduced-motion fails
